subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should cron get a dedicated `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` policy, inherit `tools.subagents.tools`, or wait for the broader per-session tool-policy design to define the cron boundary?
rationale: This changes a public config surface and hard tool-execution boundary for scheduled automation, and cleanup automation should not choose the precedence or default security guarantee.

options.title: Design cron policy in the session-policy model
options.body: Use the per-session/capability-profile direction to define cron precedence first, then add cron enforcement, docs, and tests on that canonical path.

options.title: Add a dedicated cron scope now
options.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.*` as a narrow global cron policy with explicit precedence where deny wins over per-job allowlists.

options.title: Document per-job tools only
options.body: Decline a global cron policy and make per-job `--tools` plus delivery safeguards the supported operator workflow.

recommendation.title: Design cron policy in the session-policy model
recommendation.body: Use the per-session/capability-profile direction to define cron precedence first, then add cron enforcement, docs, and tests on that canonical path.

likelyOwner.reason: He previously reviewed this issue and has recent history in the cron/session capability paths that frame the product/security choice.
